summary: In this excerpt from Book 15, Amah, the elderly matriarch of the Whiston family, confronts Ray Marlowe about his relationship with Emma. She tells him that respect is required of anyone who wants to come close to the family, and that the Whistons do not change even as times do. Emma then announces she is leaving to return to the children's afternoon lessons, and Ray, reluctant to make Emma bear the weight of his conflicting interests again, does not argue or get angry.
one_line: Amah, matriarch of the Whiston family, warns Ray Marlowe about respecting the family while Emma prepares to leave with him.
key_facts: Amah tells Ray Marlowe that it is not her place to tell a girl of Emma's age how to conduct her affairs.
Amah says that she measures by standards that are no longer in fashion.
Amah tells Ray: "Times change, Mr. Marlowe. Standards change. But the Whistons do not."
Amah says that what is demanded of those who would flutter near to the Whiston family's flame is respect.
Amah tells Ray that perhaps in time he will come to see this is true, if he has the fortitude to endure.
Emma tells Amah: "Ray just wants to take me to lunch."
Amah asks Ray: "Is that what you want, Mr. Marlowe?"
Ray answers "If you don't mind," and Amah replies "None of my business."
Emma says "Then I think I'll go," in hardly more than a whisper.
Emma says the children have been fed and Leela is putting the younger ones down for their nap.
Emma says she should be back in time for the children's afternoon lessons.
Amah says she trusts Mr. Marlowe will help Emma keep track of the time and return her "in decent order."
Ray does not get angry because he has already forced Emma to bear the weight of his conflicting interests once and will not do it again.
Ray reflects that he is starting to remember why it seemed easier to pay for sex than to pursue Air Force women who wanted relationships.
Emma kisses Amah's cheek warmly and Amah embraces her before Emma disentangles herself.

entities.name: Ray Marlowe
entities.role: Male protagonist, addressed as Mr. Marlowe, a former sergeant and 'man of the world' who is courting Emma and is being questioned by Amah

entities.name: Emma
entities.role: Young woman who cares for the children, Ray's companion, who wants to take a lunch outing and leaves to return for the afternoon lessons

entities.name: Amah
entities.role: Elderly matriarch of the Whiston family who questions Ray's intentions and insists on respect for the family's ways

entities.name: The Whistons
entities.role: The family whose old and strange ways Amah defends and whose standards do not change

entities.name: Leela
entities.role: Helper who is putting the younger children down for their nap

entities.name: Air Force
entities.role: Service branch whose women Ray compares unfavorably with paid companions because they are relationship-minded
